name: Konark Sun Temple

name: Barabati Fort

name: Daringbadi
description: Odisha's hill-station oddity at around 3,000 ft: pine groves, coffee gardens and some of the state's coolest winter nights. The surrounding Kandhamal hills double as a scenic drive.
insider_tip: Dec–Jan is frost season; small local homestays beat the big resorts.

name: Ancient site of Asurgarh fort
description: Asurgarh is an archaeological site in the Kalahandi district of Odisha, India. Asurgarh is one of the sites which has its beginning in around 5th century BCE to 5th century AD and emerged as one of the early urban fortified settlements in the region and it is older than Sisupalgarh. Pre-Mauryan, Mauryan and Gupta period coins are found in large number, these coins, discovered at Asurgarh, are categorized into two groups: 69 belong to the pre-Mauryan period, while 272 are from the Mauryan epoch and Gupta period.

name: Prehistoric sites
description: Mayurbhanj district is one of the 30 districts of Odisha state in eastern India and the largest in the state by area, nearly equivalent to Tripura. The district's headquarters is located in Baripada, with other major towns including Rairangpur, Karanjia, and Udala. As of 2011, Mayurbhanj ranks as the third-most populous district in Odisha, following Ganjam and Cuttack.

name: Panchalingeswar Hill View
description: Five lingas lie bathed by a mountain stream on this forested hill near Nilagiri — pilgrims wade upstream to reach them. A shrine that doubles as a creek-side mini-trek.
insider_tip: Carry footwear you can take off — the path is in shallow water most of the year.

name: Mangalajodi Wetlands
description: A wetland village on Chilika's northern edge where former bird poachers now work as protectors and boat guides — one of India's best community-conservation stories. Winter dawns bring thousands of migratory waders within a canoe's length.
insider_tip: Book the dawn boat through the village ecotourism counter; Nov–Feb is peak birding season.

name: Deomali Peak
description: Odisha's highest peak (around 1,672 m) — a roll of green hills and tribal villages in Koraput. The drive up is as much the attraction as the summit panorama.
insider_tip: Time it for sunset; combine with Koraput's Parab festival (Nov–Dec).

name: Hirakud Dam
description: One of the world's longest earthen dams (about 26 km) holding back the Mahanadi near Sambalpur. The dyke-top drive and the Gandhi Minar tower views are quintessentially Odia.
insider_tip: Sunset from Gandhi Minar; monsoon-season water releases are dramatic.
